title: Module 1: Application Development Overview
description: Application development concepts, technical fit, the scoped application model, development vs. deployment, JavaScript modes, and required skills.

questions.prompt: What is at the core/foundation of the ServiceNow platform?

choices.text: A NoSQL document store
A relational database
A graphics rendering engine
A file-based storage system

questions.explanation: ServiceNow is an aPaaS built on a relational database at its core.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a ServiceNow cloud-based application is correct?

choices.text: Each user must install an executable client module.
The customer is responsible for hosting the hardware.
Nothing to install; it is delivered over the internet and used through a web browser.
It can only ever be accessed through a dedicated ServiceNow desktop application client.

questions.explanation: Cloud-based: nothing to install, delivered over the internet via a browser; ServiceNow manages the hardware.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are characteristics of a process that is a **good** technical fit for a ServiceNow application? (Choose 3)

choices.text: The process follows a "request-fulfill" pattern.
The data is primarily unstructured streaming media.
The data can be modeled in a relational database.
The process needs workflows/flows to manage it and reporting capability.

questions.explanation: A request-fulfill pattern, relational-modelable data, and the need for flows/reporting are all good-fit signs. Unstructured streaming media is a bad-fit characteristic.

questions.prompt: A team wants to build an application whose core feature is streaming live video with a real-time multiplayer graphics engine. Why is this a **bad** technical fit for ServiceNow?

choices.text: ServiceNow is fundamentally incapable of storing binary data such as large video files.
The data is unstructured and the app requires a graphics engine, with no clear process flow.
ServiceNow does not support JavaScript.
ServiceNow applications cannot use forms.

questions.explanation: Unstructured data + graphics engine + no process flow are all bad-fit indicators.

questions.prompt: A developer saves a new custom application record with a chosen scope. The next day they want to move that application from its private scope into the global scope. What is true?

choices.text: They are free to change the application's scope at any time from the application record itself.
An application's scope cannot be changed once the record is saved to the database.
They can only change the scope if they currently hold the platform admin role on the instance.
Scope can be changed, but only within the first 24 hours immediately after the app's creation.

questions.explanation: Scope cannot be changed once the record is saved; there is no migration path.

questions.prompt: Which scope contains baseline applications and custom applications that were built on ServiceNow versions prior to scoping?

choices.text: Private scope
Delegated scope
Global scope
System scope

questions.explanation: Global scope: baseline apps + custom apps built before scoping.

questions.prompt: Which capability is available to **scoped** applications but **not** to global applications?

choices.text: Publish to the application repository
Easy file management
Delegated Development
Use of business rules

questions.explanation: Delegated Development is unique to scoped apps. (Repository publish and file management are available to both.)

questions.prompt: A scoped application namespace identifier is `x_acme_book_rooms`. Which statements about scope namespaces are correct? (Choose 3)

choices.text: All scoped application namespaces begin with the `x_` prefix.
The company code (`acme` here) comes from the `glide.appcreator.company.code` system property and is 2 to 5 characters long.
The total namespace identifier can be at most 18 characters long.
The company code is chosen freely by the developer at app-creation time.

questions.explanation: The x_ prefix, a 2-to-5 character company code from glide.appcreator.company.code, and an 18-character total maximum are all correct. The company code is generated by ServiceNow per customer, not chosen freely by the developer.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended best practice for where to develop new functionality?

choices.text: Always in the global scope
In a private scoped application
In a personal developer instance only
In Compatibility Mode scripts

questions.explanation: Best practice is to develop in a private scoped application.

questions.prompt: In the **baseline** configuration, what database access does one custom (scoped) application have to another custom application's table records?

choices.text: By default it has full read and write access to all of the other app's records
Read access only; no other DB operations without explicit configuration
No database access of any kind at all without explicit cross-scope configuration first
Write access only

questions.explanation: Baseline: read access to other apps' table records only; no other DB operations without explicit configuration.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are common, legitimate reasons to build in the **global** scope instead of a private scope? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Modifications to legacy customizations already done in global.
Changes to base instance code that exists in global.
Building a brand-new, self-contained utility application.
Access is required to global application files that is not available to scoped applications.

questions.explanation: Legacy global modifications, base instance code changes, and needing access to global-only files are valid reasons to build in global. Building a brand-new, self-contained utility application is a textbook scoped-app case, not a global one.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Delegated Development is correct?

choices.text: Delegated access can be granted to both global and scoped applications.
Delegated access can be granted only to scoped applications.
Delegated developers automatically have permissions across every application.
Delegated Development requires the user to already have the admin role.

questions.explanation: Delegated access can be granted only to scoped applications.

questions.prompt: An admin wants a non-admin developer to be able to create advanced business rules (which contain scripts) in a scoped application. Which two developer permissions does that developer need? (Choose 2)

choices.text: All File Types
Allow Scripting
Security Admin
Publish to Store

questions.explanation: All File Types + Allow Scripting are both required to create advanced (scripted) business rules.

questions.prompt: Which tools can be used to **deploy** a completed application? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Update Sets
Application Repository
ServiceNow Store
Mozilla Rhino

questions.explanation: Update Sets, Application Repository, and ServiceNow Store are deployment options. (Mozilla Rhino is the server-side JS engine, not a deployment tool.)

questions.prompt: During the **development** process (saving incremental work), what does ServiceNow Studio use to track contributions?

choices.text: Git commits
Update Sets
The ServiceNow Store
Flow Designer

questions.explanation: Studio uses named incremental Update Sets to track development.

questions.prompt: What is the **default** JavaScript mode for new server-side scripts in current ServiceNow releases?

choices.text: Compatibility Mode
ES5 Standards Mode
ECMAScript 2021 (ES12)
ECMAScript 5.1 Legacy Mode

questions.explanation: ECMAScript 2021 (ES12) is the default mode.

questions.prompt: Which statements about JavaScript modes in ServiceNow are correct? (Choose 2)

choices.text: Compatibility Mode is used for all scripts developed before the Helsinki release and for all global scripts.
Third-party JavaScript libraries are fully supported in Compatibility Mode.
ECMAScript 2021 (ES12) supports features such as `let`, `const`, default function parameters, and `for-of` loops.
ES5 Standards Mode is the default mode for all new applications.

questions.explanation: Compatibility Mode covers pre-Helsinki and all global scripts, and ES12 supports let/const/default parameters/for-of loops. Note: third-party JavaScript libraries are NOT supported in Compatibility Mode, and ES12 (not ES5) is the default mode.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between the ServiceNow **Store** and the **Developer Share** site?

choices.text: The Store is free, while Developer Share apps always cost money.
Store apps are vetted and supported (may cost money); Developer Share apps are free, unvetted.
Developer Share apps are vetted by ServiceNow first, while Store apps are not vetted.
Both are vetted identically; the only difference is the URL.

questions.explanation: Store = vetted + supported (may cost money); Developer Share = free + not vetted.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the **philosophy of scoped apps**?

choices.text: Scope makes applications run faster by caching their records in memory.
Scope protects an app from damaging or being damaged by others; out-of-scope access must be explicitly configured.
Scope automatically grants every single application full admin-level access to all of the tables on the entire instance.
Scope removes the need for access controls within an application.

questions.explanation: Scope shields apps from each other; out-of-scope access must be explicitly configured.

questions.prompt: What does the term **artifact** refer to in the context of a scoped application?

choices.text: A deprecated, leftover application file that is no longer in use and should be deleted soon.
Any of the application files that make up an app (ACLs, business rules, tables), within its scope.
A backup copy of the application stored in the repository.
A record that exists only in the global scope.

questions.explanation: Artifacts are the application files that make up an app, living within its scope.
